messages:
Alex P: Quick follow-up from the shadow-relay spike — proposing a cleanup/cutover plan for the minimal control-plane shadow relay. Goal: remove legacy per-tenant connector route while keeping egress IP preservation and fast rollback if we see src-IP shifts.
Maria G: Nice. Can you outline the rollback criteria and the canary windows?
Alex P: TL;DR plan below. Canary = 5% of tenants for 24h, then 25% for 12h, then 100% if no regressions. Rollback triggers: >=1% requests with src-ip-preservation failure, or p50 latency regressed >50ms vs baseline, or 5% increase in 5xx.
Jon S: How are we measuring "src-ip-preservation failure"? We need a tight definition.
Alex P: We compare observed source IP at egress vs expected tenant IP mapping. If an active session's observed_srcip != expected_srcip for more than 30s and request count > 10, mark as failed. Metric name: relay.srcip.mismatch.rate.
Kevin L: Are we changing SNAT behavior? Legacy connector preserved srcip by hairpinning; shadow-relay mirrors flow state and relies on ephemeral SNAT pools. That worries ops.
Alex P: We do not change tenant-visible source IP for canary tenants. Shadow-relay will program a NAT-exempt rule for flows matched by tenancy tag until stable cutover. Implementation sketch: 
```bash
# operator: pin flow to shadow-relay path
kubectl patch configmap tenant-egress-rules -p '{"data":{"tenant-123":"no-snat"}}'
```
Maria G: That patch approach seems risky at scale. What about using route-policy with per-tenant mark instead?
Jon S: Route-policy would be cleaner: set connmark on inbound, relay honors connmark and disables SNAT for marked flows. Fallback flow: if shadow-relay not responsive, connmark expires and default SNAT resumes.
Alex P: Good call. We'll prototype connmark + conntrack-check. Also adding health probe: /_relay_health that returns active mapping count, and kill switch endpoint to immediately re-enable SNAT globally.
Kevin L: Observability needs: tokenized query to see affected tenants and list of flows. Suggest adding these logs to cp-trace-index with tenant_id label so queries are simple.
Alex P: Agreed. Metrics to add: relay.connmark.set.count, relay.connmark.expire.count, relay.srcip.mismatch.rate, relay.health.status. Dashboards: Canary view with per-tenant rows.
Maria G: What about certs for relay handshakes? During spike we used short-lived client certs. For production we need rotation plan.
Alex P: Rotation plan: CA-signed certs with 24h TTL for canary, automated rotation via operator every 20h. Rollback: set operator to keep previous cert for 48h. Also add audit log entries on cert renewals.
Jon S: Any config that we need to distribute to Dedicated or Private customers? This seems like network-level changes that some customers control.
Alex P: For Private deployments we will ship the same relay agent but with a default config that preserves tenant-owned egress by default. The cutover will be opt-in for Private; Hosted/Dedicated will be opt-out.
Kevin L: Timelines? I want a migration window that hits low-traffic hours for each region.
Alex P: Proposed schedule: Staging rollout Mon, Canary (5%) Tue 00:00 UTC -> Wed 00:00 UTC, 25% Wed 02:00 -> Wed 14:00, Full Thursday 02:00 if green. Buffer Friday for cleanup.
Maria G: Who's owning the canary operator run? Need an oncall and escalation.
Alex P: Owners: Jon S (primary), Kevin L (secondary). Escalation: paging rotation -> oncall-net. I'll add runbook steps.
Jon S: Runbook snippets: 1) Query relay.srcip.mismatch.rate for canary tenants 2) If mismatch >0.5% over 15m, hit kill switch: POST /relay/admin/kill-switch -> re-enable SNAT 3) Roll back routing entries and deploy previous operator image.
Maria G: Add a step to validate outbound IPs with curl from tenant simulator and compare to recorded mapping.
Alex P: Good. We'll include a small k6 test: 1000 connections, sample egress ip, compare.
Kevin L: Any DB schema changes for storing tenant flow marks? If so, migrations can be hairy.
Alex P: No persistent DB changes — connmark is ephemeral and stored in agent memory/conntrack. We will write mapping to cp-cache (in-memory) with TTL so no durable migration needed.
Jon S: Are we expecting to deprecate the old connector agent? If so, include compatibility shim for next 2 quarters.
Alex P: Yes: deprecation plan: 3-month transition. Phase 1 (0-1m) shadow-only, phase 2 (1-2m) encourage tenants to opt-in to new path, phase 3 (2-3m) remove legacy. But we keep a compatibility flag for enterprise customers; can extend on request.
Maria G: Security review? I want a quick sec check for connmark spoofing or privilege escalation.
Kevin L: Connmark should be set only by authenticated relay handshake. Use mTLS client certs + per-tenant signing. Add attestation check for path origin in handshake.
Alex P: Noted. I'll open a sec checklist item: require mTLS mutual auth, handshake attestation, and rate-limit connmark ops per agent.
deploy-bot: Scheduled relay-canary deployment: 2026-03-28T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-29T00:00:00Z (canary 5%). Owner: Jon S. :rocket:
Maria G: OK let's run the staging tests early next week and then proceed. I'll review the dashboard and sign off after 24h of canary metrics.
Jon S: I'll prepare the runbook and load the k6 scripts into infra-tests repo.
Alex P: Thanks everyone. I'll post a short RFC update and attach the runbook and metrics queries. :thumbsup:
